findings.summary: Every page is titled and heroed for the topic it finishes rather than the topic it spends most of its space teaching, so a learner scanning headers is consistently pointed at the wrong subject.
findings.evidence: Page 8 is "page_title":"AWS Database Services","hero":"rds","subtitle":"RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache" yet contains only ELB, "1. Route 53 (DNS Service)", "3. CloudFront (CDN)", "4. VPC Peering", "5. Transit Gateway", "6. VPN Connection", "1. The Hero Mark" and "4. The Motto" — no database block at all. Page 5 is titled "Compute Services" but carries VPC, Route 53, ELB, CloudFront, Direct Connect and VPN; page 6 is titled "Networking Services" but carries S3, EBS, EFS, FSx, Glacier and Storage Gateway; page 4 keeps "hero":"rds","subtitle":"Managed Databases for Workloads" while teaching EC2 through Batch.
findings.fix: Re-title, re-hero and re-subtitle each page after the material that dominates it (page 5 → Networking, page 6 → Storage, page 8 → Advanced Networking + Handbook Identity), or repaginate so each topic's sections start at the top of the page that bears its name.

findings.summary: The title "AWS Database Services" names a topic that does not appear anywhere on the page, which is entirely networking plus brand identity.
findings.evidence: Page 8 blocks are "1. Route 53 (DNS Service)", "3. CloudFront (CDN)", "4. VPC Peering", "5. Transit Gateway", "6. VPN Connection", "1. The Hero Mark", "4. The Motto" — no RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB or ElastiCache content (the page's subtitle also still reads "RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache").
findings.fix: Retitle page 8 to "Networking: Peering, Transit Gateway & VPN" and change its subtitle from "RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache" to match (e.g. "Connect VPCs and On-Prem").

findings.summary: Page titles, subtitles and hero marks are systematically off by one page relative to the content they sit on.
findings.evidence: Page 5 is titled "Compute Services" but its blocks are "1. VPC", "2. Route 53", "3. Elastic Load Balancing", "4. CloudFront", "5. Direct Connect", "6. VPN"; page 6 is titled "Networking Services" but its blocks are S3/EBS/EFS/FSx/S3 Glacier/Storage Gateway; page 8 is titled "AWS Database Services" with subtitle "RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache" and hero "rds", but contains Route 53, CloudFront, VPC Peering, Transit Gateway, VPN and brand-identity blocks.
findings.fix: Re-map each page's title/subtitle/hero to the services actually on it (p4 "Compute Basics" not hero "rds"/"Managed Databases for Workloads"; p5 → Networking; p6 → Storage; p8 → Networking + Handbook Identity), or re-flow the blocks so they land under the matching heading after the spill from Part 1.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a part label rather than a hook, so the feed preview opens with no reason to stop scrolling.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of AWS COMPLETE NOTES. Master AWS from Beginner to Advanced with this complete handwritten-notes handbook."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and demote the part label: "Master AWS from beginner to advanced — IAM, EC2, S3, VPC and more in one handwritten-notes handbook. (Part 2 of AWS COMPLETE NOTES.)"

findings.summary: The SG vs NACL "Default" row is wrong for security groups and contradicts the equivalent table on page 7.
findings.evidence: ["Default","Deny all","Allow all"] — while page 7's table states ["Default","Allow all outbound","Deny all"].
findings.fix: State it precisely in both tables: a newly created security group denies all inbound and allows all outbound; the VPC's default network ACL allows all inbound and outbound, while a custom network ACL denies all until rules are added.

findings.summary: The CloudFormation process diagram is placed a page ahead of the CloudFormation section that explains it.
findings.evidence: Page 1 contains a flow with nodes ["Template (JSON/YAML)","CloudFormation Stack","AWS Resources"] sitting between "3. AWS Config" and "6. Trusted Advisor", with no heading; "5. CloudFormation" and its bullets ("Infrastructure as Code (IaC)") are on page 2.
findings.fix: Move the template-to-stack diagram to page 2, directly under the "5. CloudFormation" bullets.

findings.summary: Trusted Advisor asserts "5 pillars" with no list, and the list itself lands on the next page detached from the section it belongs to.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "6. Trusted Advisor" / "Checks across 5 pillars" with no enumeration; page 2 carries a stray sidebox "Trusted Advisor Pillars" (Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, Service Limits) placed after the CloudFormation bullets.
findings.fix: Pair the pillars sidebox with the "6. Trusted Advisor" bullets on the same page.

findings.summary: The Aurora architecture diagram appears a page before Aurora is defined.
findings.evidence: Page 2's final block is a flow with nodes ["Application","Aurora Primary","Aurora Storage","Aurora Replica","Aurora Replica"]; the heading "3. Aurora" and its bullets ("MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible", "Up to 5x performance of standard MySQL") are on page 3.
findings.fix: Move the Aurora flow diagram to page 3, directly beneath the "3. Aurora" bullets.

findings.summary: Three compute diagrams close page 3 before any of the compute services in them have been introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ends with flows ["User","EC2","EBS Volume","Security Group"], ["S3 Bucket","Lambda Function","DynamoDB"] and ["Docker","ECS Cluster","Task","ECR"]; the headings "1. EC2", "2. Lambda" and "3. ECS" only appear on page 4.
findings.fix: Move each diagram onto page 4 immediately after its own numbered section.

findings.summary: The compute comparison table claims AWS manages Lightsail, ECS and EKS, which misstates who owns the OS and node layer.
findings.evidence: ["ECS","Containers","AWS manages"], ["EKS","Kubernetes","AWS manages"], ["Lightsail","VPS","AWS manages"]
findings.fix: Change Lightsail to "You manage the OS" (a Lightsail instance is a VM you patch and administer), ECS to "AWS manages the control plane; you manage EC2 capacity unless using Fargate", and EKS to "AWS manages the control plane; you manage worker nodes unless using Fargate/Auto Mode".

findings.summary: The title "Compute Services" misdescribes a page that is networking content after its first block.
findings.evidence: Page 5 opens with one compute recap ("8. Use Cases" — "EC2: web servers…", "Lambda: image resizing…") then covers "1. VPC", "2. Route 53", "3. Elastic Load Balancing", "4. CloudFront", "5. Direct Connect", "6. VPN", "7. Comparison", "8. Security in Networking".
findings.fix: Retitle page 5 to "Networking Services: VPC to VPN".

findings.summary: Storage "10. Best Practices" is taught a full page before the comparison, feature summary and storage-class table it is meant to summarise.
findings.evidence: Page 6 ends with "10. Best Practices" / "Choose the right storage service"; page 7 then opens with "7. Comparison", "8. Key Features" and "9. S3 Storage Classes" — the table that actually tells the learner which service to choose.
findings.fix: Move sections 7, 8 and 9 ahead of section 10 so the best-practice list closes the storage sequence instead of opening it.

findings.summary: The title "Networking Services" misdescribes a page whose body is almost entirely storage services.
findings.evidence: After two networking wrap-up blocks ("9. Use Cases", "10. Key Takeaways"), page 6 runs "1. S3", "2. EBS", "3. EFS", "4. FSx", "5. S3 Glacier", "6. Storage Gateway", "10. Best Practices" with the lead-in "A range of storage services to ==store, secure and retrieve== data in the cloud."
findings.fix: Retitle page 6 to "Storage Services: S3 to Glacier" (and move the "Networking Services" title back onto the page that actually carries VPC/Route 53/ELB).

findings.summary: The storage comparison table mislabels 99.999% as "4 9s" and applies io2-only durability to all of EBS.
findings.fix: Change the EBS durability cell to "99.8–99.9% (io2 Block Express: 99.999%)" and drop the "(4 9s)" label — 99.999% is five nines, and AWS documents 99.8%–99.9% durability (0.1–0.2% AFR) for gp2/gp3/io1/st1/sc1.

findings.summary: The storage page ends by jumping back to networking sections numbered 3 and 6, re-teaching VPC material two pages after VPC was introduced.
findings.evidence: After "9. S3 Storage Classes", page 7 continues with "3. VPC Architecture (Example)" (flowchart "VPC 10.0.0.0/16" with public/private subnets, IGW and NAT), "6. Security Group vs Network ACL", and a "DNS Lookup" flowchart — while "1. VPC" and "2. Route 53" were taught back on page 5.
findings.fix: Move the VPC architecture flowchart, the SG vs NACL table and the DNS lookup diagram back into the networking sequence on page 5, next to their numbered sections.

findings.summary: The second SG vs NACL table directly contradicts the first one on the default-rule row.
findings.evidence: Page 1 table row ["Default","Deny all","Allow all"] (SG deny all, NACL allow all); page 7 table row ["Default","Allow all outbound","Deny all"] (SG allow all outbound, NACL deny all).
findings.fix: Keep one SG vs NACL table and state the default precisely: a security group denies all inbound and allows all outbound; the default NACL allows all traffic while a newly created custom NACL denies all.

findings.summary: Route 53 and CloudFront are introduced from scratch a second time, three pages after they were already taught, and the page opens with an ELB diagram that has no heading anywhere in the part.
findings.evidence: Page 8 has "1. Route 53 (DNS Service)" and "3. CloudFront (CDN)" with definitional bullets ("Scalable ==DNS==: converts domain names to IP addresses", "==CDN== with low latency"), but page 5 already carried "2. Route 53" and "4. CloudFront"; page 8's first block is the "ELB" flowchart with no "2. Elastic Load Balancing" heading preceding it.
findings.fix: Fold the advanced networking sections (peering, Transit Gateway, VPN) into the page 5 networking run as continuations rather than re-definitions, and either restore the missing ELB heading or drop the orphaned ELB diagram.

findings.summary: The handbook-identity sequence is presented out of numeric order across two pages, with section 4 taught before sections 2 and 3.
findings.evidence: Page 8 ends with "1. The Hero Mark" then "4. The Motto"; page 9 then gives "2. Why a Cloud Mark", "3. Mark Rules" and only afterwards "5. Motto Stages".
findings.fix: Move "4. The Motto" onto page 9 after "3. Mark Rules" so the identity run reads 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

findings.summary: Trusted Advisor is described as checking 5 pillars; it now has six check categories.
findings.evidence: "Improves security, performance, cost optimization", "Checks across 5 pillars"
findings.fix: Say "Checks across 6 categories" and name them: Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance (Resilience), Service Limits, Operational Excellence.

findings.summary: Section 7 of the security page (encryption options) is missing entirely, yet encryption at rest/in transit and KMS are asserted as requirements later without ever being explained.
findings.evidence: Page 1 runs "5. Key Security Services" → "6. SG vs NACL" → "8. Common Mistakes"; the only KMS mention is the table row ["KMS","Manage encryption keys"], while page 4 ("Encrypt at rest and in transit") and page 6 ("Encrypt at rest and in transit", "MFA delete for critical buckets") depend on it.
findings.fix: Restore the syllabus's "7. Encryption Options" section (data at rest on EBS/S3/RDS, data in transit via TLS, key management with KMS) before "8. Common Mistakes".

findings.summary: The title "Security & IAM" covers only the first third of the page; the majority is management and monitoring.
findings.evidence: Page 1 runs "5. Key Security Services", "6. SG vs NACL", "8. Common Mistakes" and then "1. CloudWatch", "2. CloudTrail", "3. AWS Config", a CloudFormation flow diagram and "6. Trusted Advisor".
findings.fix: Broaden the title to "Security, IAM & Monitoring" so it covers both halves of the page.

findings.summary: The Trusted Advisor sidebox omits the Operational Excellence category.
findings.evidence: sidebox "Trusted Advisor Pillars": ["Cost Optimization","Performance","Security","Fault Tolerance","Service Limits"]
findings.fix: Add "Operational Excellence" as a sixth item (and optionally rename "Fault Tolerance" to "Resilience", AWS's current label).

findings.summary: The title "Storage Services" covers only the first half of the page; the second half is networking.
findings.evidence: After "7. Comparison" (S3/EBS/EFS/FSx), "8. Key Features" and "9. S3 Storage Classes", page 7 continues with "3. VPC Architecture (Example)", "6. Security Group vs Network ACL" and a "DNS Lookup" flowchart.
findings.fix: Retitle page 7 to "Storage Classes & VPC Essentials", or move the three networking blocks onto a networking page.

findings.summary: The VPN section attributes IPsec to both VPN types, but AWS Client VPN is TLS/OpenVPN-based, not IPsec.
findings.evidence: "Encrypted tunnel using **IPSec**", "Types: Site-to-Site VPN, Client VPN"
findings.fix: Scope the protocol: "Site-to-Site VPN: IPsec tunnels to a virtual private gateway or transit gateway; Client VPN: TLS (OpenVPN-based) for individual users".

findings.summary: The identity section calls the AWS hero mark a cloud, but the AWS logo is the "aws" wordmark with the smile arrow and contains no cloud.
findings.evidence: "A cloud reads as {blue:cloud computing} at a glance" and "Orange smile arrow keeps the palette warm" (page 8: "The ==AWS cloud logo== is the hero mark")
findings.fix: Rewrite as "the AWS wordmark and orange smile arrow" throughout (page 8 bullet, page 9 heading "2. Why a Cloud Mark" and its first bullet), or state plainly that the hero mark is a generic cloud icon used alongside — not instead of — the AWS logo.
